text: Love the art in yourself, not yourself in the art.
context: On ego and craft — the work must be larger than the performer's vanity

text: There are no small parts, only small actors.
context: On full preparation regardless of role size

text: The physical action is the door to the inner life.
context: On using physical score to access emotional truth

text: Acting is living truthfully under imaginary circumstances.
context: Foundational definition of the craft

text: The foundation of acting is the reality of doing.
context: On committing to action rather than indicating

text: Don't do anything unless something makes you do it.
context: On reactive, earned behavior over performed behavior

text: Your talent is in your imagination.
context: The actor's primary instrument is imagination, not recalled emotion

text: Life is not what it is. It's what you make it in your imagination.
context: On elevating given circumstances through imagination

text: The word in the script is the last step in a long journey.
context: On the depth of analysis required before a single line is spoken

text: The size of your talent is the size of your choices.
context: On the direct link between bold choices and strong work

text: The actor must know why he is doing what he is doing at every moment.
context: On the necessity of specific intention in every beat

text: Find in yourself those human things which are universal.
context: On connecting personal truth to the character's circumstances

text: You have to get beyond your own precious inner experiences.
context: On moving from self-expression to communicative work

text: Every character has a psychological gesture — a single movement that expresses its entire inner life.
context: On finding the character's core through the body

text: When your imagination is alive, your body will follow.
context: On the connection between imaginative specificity and physical truth

text: The actor's instrument is himself.
context: On the obligation to continuously refine the self as an instrument

text: We do not act with our heads. We act with our entire instrument.
context: On the integration of body, emotion, and thought in performance

text: Every moment must have a reason for existing.
context: On earning each beat rather than simply executing it

text: The character's want is the engine. Without a want, there is no performance.
context: On objective as the driving force of all acting

text: The best direction is action direction. Telling an actor what to feel is useless.
context: On playable actions vs. emotional directives

text: What does the actor want? What is the actor doing? These are not poetic questions. They are technical ones.
context: On the technical precision underneath every acting choice

text: You can learn to act the same way you learn anything — by doing it over and over until you can't get it wrong.
context: On repetition, embodiment, and the path to mastery

text: The moment you decide what you want, you have already started acting.
context: On the inseparability of decision-making and performance

text: Movement does not lie. The body always tells the truth.
context: On physicality as the primary language of performance

text: The body is the score. Everything else is interpretation.
context: On the physicalized structure of performance as primary text

text: Acting is not about being someone different. It's finding the similarity in what is apparently different, then finding myself in there.
context: On the paradox of disappearing into a character

text: The moment you feel you have the luxury of coasting, that's when your work starts to die.
context: On the obligation of full investment at every stage

text: I need to find reasons to do the work. If I can't find them, I shouldn't be doing it.
context: On the necessity of genuine investment before beginning

text: You cannot get to the truth of a character without dealing with your own truth.
context: On the personal instrument as the foundation of character work

text: Actors don't have lines. They have tactics. The line is the result of the tactic.
context: On the distinction between text and intention

text: The biggest challenge of acting is to be willing to be seen.
context: On vulnerability as a technical requirement, not an emotional one

text: You have to keep breaking your heart until it opens.
context: On the ongoing personal work that precedes great performance

text: I always feel the scene is more important than the performance.
context: On serving the material rather than showcasing technique

text: The hardest thing in the world is to stop doing and start being.
context: On the distinction between performing and inhabiting

text: I never think about what I'm playing. I think about what I'm doing.
context: On action over emotion as the actor's primary focus

text: I don't think about the character. I think about the problem the character is trying to solve.
context: On objective-based approach to character construction

text: The physical commitment to a role isn't vanity — it's necessity. The body has to know before the mind does.
context: On physical preparation as a form of deep character knowledge

text: The camera sees everything. It will catch you lying before the audience will.
context: On the on-camera demand for absolute honesty

text: Preparation is the opposite of showing off.
context: On preparation as service to the material, not self-display

text: The work is the reward. If you do good work, the rest follows.
context: On craft-first orientation in a career

text: You have to want it in your body, not just your head.
context: On the physical integration of a role

text: The actor's job is to discover the character, not invent him.
context: On the distinction between exploration and construction

text: What I want from an actor is specificity. Generic choices kill scenes.
context: On the director's core demand from actors

text: I don't direct actors. I give them something to want, badly.
context: On objective as the director's primary tool with actors

text: The actor who can listen — really listen — is worth ten who can only project.
context: On listening as the most underrated technical skill

text: The human face is the most remarkable close-up there is.
context: On the camera as the ultimate tool for revealing inner life

text: I never give an actor a direction that describes an emotion. I give them something to do.
context: On action-based direction over emotional direction

text: I don't want a finished performance. I want a discovered one.
context: On the value of live discovery over polished execution

text: The best work comes from actors who don't perform — they inhabit.
context: On the distinction between performing for an audience and living inside a role

text: The camera is not interested in your performance. It is interested in your thought.
context: On interiority as the on-camera actor's primary tool

text: What I want from actors is simplicity. The camera amplifies everything.
context: On restraint and economy in on-camera performance

text: If you're acting for the audience, you're already one beat behind. Act for the scene.
context: On the difference between performing outward and living inward

text: The scene is a question. The actor's job is to answer it, not explain it.
context: On playing the scene rather than commenting on it

text: The actor's preparation is the director's pre-production. Both have to be done before you get on set.
context: On preparation as the actor's professional obligation

text: Don't explain it. Play it. The audience doesn't need your understanding — they need your action.
context: On action over analysis as the actor's fundamental orientation

text: All reading of the script is acting. The way you read it is the way you play it.
context: On the inseparability of analysis and performance

text: There are two silences. One when no word is spoken. The other when perhaps a torrent of language is being employed.
context: On subtext as the primary content of dramatic speech

text: If in the first act you have hung a pistol on the wall, then in the following one it should be fired.
context: On structural inevitability — every action must earn its consequence

text: I don't want realism. I want magic — and I try to give that to people. I misrepresent such things as beauty and desire and romance — but who doesn't? And if that is sinful, then let me be damned for it.
context: On the obligation to reach beyond surface realism toward emotional truth

text: A good play is one that asks an actor to solve a real human problem.
context: On the actor's work as problem-solving, not decoration

text: The character is the playwright's skeleton. The actor adds the flesh.
context: On the actor's unique creative contribution to a written role

text: The actor who doesn't know where they come from can't know where the character is going.
context: On history and context as essential preparation

text: Actors who study are better than actors who don't. That's the only rule.
context: On continuous training as the irreducible professional standard

text: The most complex thing in drama is a human being who wants something.
context: On want/objective as the engine of all dramatic action

text: A man walks across an empty space whilst someone else is watching him — that is all that is needed for an act of theatre.
context: On presence as the irreducible element of performance

text: The actor must show that his character's behavior is chosen, not inevitable.
context: On demonstrating agency and choice in every action

text: Light isn't decoration. It's where the scene lives.
context: On atmosphere and environment as active participants in performance

text: Shadow is not the absence of light. It is the most powerful light you have.
context: On what is withheld being as powerful as what is revealed — true for acting too

text: Simplicity of light is the hardest thing to achieve. The same is true of acting.
context: On economy and clarity as the highest form of craft

text: You can feel when an actor is inside the moment. The frame knows.
context: On presence as something the camera detects before the audience does

text: The camera is always honest. If the actor isn't present, the camera is the first to know.
context: On the unforgiving nature of on-camera work
